mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months, it signals monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals an overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) above 5% YoY compresses equity risk premiums, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances during late-cycle expansion despite RSAFS growth >5% YoY, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters, it signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% YoY for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months, it signals tight labor market conditions that boost corporate profits, causing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in >60% of instances where UNRATE is below 4.0% for three consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105.0 (index 2017=100) indicates strong manufacturing activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 105.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery, a sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200.0 thousand units signals improving consumer confidence, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in >60% of instances during post-recession recovery despite HOUST above 1200.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
